'''Bernard Kirtman''' (born March 30, 1935)<ref name="a">{{Cite web|url=https://dailynexus.com/2017-09-28/oldest-ucsb-prof-taught-through-vietnam-civil-rights-movement/|title=Oldest UCSB Prof. Taught Through Vietnam, Civil Rights Movement|work=[[Daily Nexus]]|date=September 28, 2017|first=Maura|last=Fox|access-date=June 6, 2026}}</ref> is an American [[Theoretical chemistry|theoretical chemist]].<ref name="c" /><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/First_UCSB_Conference_on_Effective_Teach/tTY8AAAAIAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=0&bsq=bernard%20kirtman%20theoretical%20chemist|title=First UCSB Conference on Effective Teaching|page=43|editor=Glasman, Naftaly S., Nicholson, Stanley J.|publisher=Learning Resources, University of California|date=1973|via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref> He is a [[distinguished professor]] in the department of [[chemistry]] and [[biochemistry]] at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]].<ref name="b">{{Cite web|url=https://www.chem.ucsb.edu/people/bernard-kirtman|title=Bernard Kirtman|work=[[University of California, Santa Barbara]]|access-date=June 6, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chem.ucsb.edu/people|title=Faculty: Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry|work=[[University of California, Santa Barbara]]|access-date=June 6, 2026}}</ref>

Kirtman attended [[Columbia University]], earning his [[Bachelor of Arts|AB degree]] in 1955.<ref>{{Citation|title=Directory of Graduate Research|page=82|author=American Chemical Society. Committee on Professional Training|date=1979}}</ref> He also attended [[Harvard University]], earning his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD degree]] in [[physical chemistry]] in 1961. After earning his degrees, he worked as a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral fellow]] at the [[University of Washington]].<ref name="b" />

In 2005, Kirtman was awarded the ICCMSE Prize for theoretical and [[computational chemistry]] by the [[Computational science|International Conference on Computational Methods and Sustainable Engineering]].<ref name="b" />
